landing.heroTitle: Every person deserves a voice that keeps up with their life.
landing.heroBody: AAC apps turn taps, switches, or gaze into spoken language — at home, in therapy, and in class. Voxa is a modern communication board with motor planning, CVI-friendly themes, word suggestions, switch scanning, visual schedules, and secure cloud sync — designed so families start free and institutions scale with confidence.
landing.whyChangingList1: Reduces frustration when speech alone is not enough
landing.whyChangingList2: Supports language development, not just request-and-response
landing.whyChangingList3: Builds independence for meals, play, medical visits, and friendships
landing.whyChangingList4: Gives caregivers and clinicians a shared, evidence-aligned tool
landing.whyChangingNote: Research consistently shows early, robust AAC access improves communication outcomes — not delays speech.
landing.humanRightBody: Digital AAC replaces paper boards with speech output, vocabulary that grows with the user, and access methods matched to physical ability. Voxa focuses on what practitioners and families ask for most: stable motor plans and visually accessible layouts.
landing.demoCtaBody: Explore core vocabulary with symbols, literacy keyboard, visual schedules, and access modes (switch scan + touch guard) — no signup required.
landing.pricingSubtitle: Always free for individual parents. Institutional plans fund secure hosting and analytics for teams.
landing.priceClinicDetail: Total includes 16% IVA · {base}/mo org + {seat}/seat before IVA (min. {minSeats})
landing.parentsBody: Forever free for individual families supporting one communicator at home.
landing.familyBody: More boards for different places and routines.
landing.instBody: Paid plan for schools, clinics, and districts that need unlimited boards. Book a call to plan the rollout.
landing.footerCtaTitle: Start where you are. Grow when you need to.
landing.footerCtaBody: Try the demo as a visitor, create a free parent account in minutes, or talk with us about rolling Voxa out across your organization.

motor.title: Motor planning first
motor.body: Core words stay in fixed locations so users build muscle memory — the same principle behind leading dedicated AAC devices.

cvi.title: CVI & access modes
cvi.body: High-contrast themes, switch scanning, and pointer dwell selection mean the same board adapts to cortical visual impairment and different physical access.

voices.title: Device voices, tuned to you
voices.body: Choose among the voices installed on the phone, tablet or computer and adjust rate, pitch and volume. Natural child voices are pending.

ai.title: Suggestions with consent
ai.body: Optional word suggestions speed up multi-word messages; families decide whether to turn them on.

obf.title: Open Board Format
obf.body: Import and export OBF to collaborate with SLPs and migrate from other apps without lock-in.

offline.title: Rides out network drops
offline.body: If the Wi‑Fi drops, the open board keeps working. Once you have opened the app with a connection, it also reopens offline on that device, with the boards you already loaded. Changes sync when the connection returns.

janua.title: Janua identity
janua.body: One MADFAM sign-in across Voxa and partner tools — fewer passwords for caregivers and staff.

firstMessage.title: You just spoke with Voxa
firstMessage.body: AAC gives non-speaking and minimally speaking people a voice for everyday needs, relationships, and learning. Create a free parent account to save boards, sync across devices, and personalize vocabulary.

templates.title: Four starter templates in the full app
templates.body: Core 47, Core 100, literacy keyboard, and visual schedules ship as editable templates — plus OBF/OBZ import in the SLP editor, and Grid 3, Snap and TouchChat import (beta — imports the words of one page).

access.title: Clinical access modes built in
access.body: Switch scanning with auditory cues, touch guard overlays, dwell selection (for head pointers and eye trackers that move the pointer), and touch-release activation — configurable per communicator in Settings.

institution.title: Plans for schools and clinics
institution.body: The institutional plan adds unlimited boards. Book a call to plan a rollout in your organization.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Voxa is an augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) platform operated by MADFAM. This policy describes how we collect, use, and protect information when you use voxa.madfam.io and related services.

sections.title: Information we collect
sections.content: We collect account information from Janua SSO (name, email, user id), communication board data you create or sync, optional usage telemetry if you opt in, and standard service logs (IP address, user agent, request timestamps) for security and reliability.

sections.title: How we use information
sections.content: We use your data to provide AAC board sync, team collaboration, accessibility features, and optional AI-assisted predictions. We do not sell utterance or board data to third parties. AI features send only the minimum context required and only when you have opted in.

sections.title: Children and guardians
sections.content: Voxa may be used by minors with guardian or clinician oversight. Account creation and billing are managed by adults. We do not knowingly collect marketing profiles on children. Guardians may request access, correction, or deletion of a dependent’s board data by contacting us.

sections.title: Data storage and retention
sections.content: Board data is stored in encrypted PostgreSQL in our cloud infrastructure. You may export boards in Open Board Format (OBF). We retain data while your account is active and for a limited period after closure for backup integrity, unless law requires longer retention.

sections.title: Sharing
sections.content: We share data only with infrastructure providers (hosting, identity, payment when applicable) under contract, or when required by law. Clinical records belong in your healthcare provider’s systems — Voxa is a communication tool, not an electronic health record.

sections.title: Your choices
sections.content: You can opt out of AI telemetry in Settings. You can export or delete boards where your role permits. You may sign out at any time to end your browser session.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: We use TLS in transit, access controls, and MADFAM platform security practices. No method is 100% secure; report concerns to hola@madfam.io.

sections.title: Changes
sections.content: We will post updates on this page with a revised “Last updated” date. Material changes may be notified by email or in-product notice.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of Voxa at voxa.madfam.io and related MADFAM services. By using Voxa, you agree to these terms.

sections.title: Service description
sections.content: Voxa provides cloud-synced AAC communication boards, team editing for caregivers and SLPs, accessibility modes, and optional AI-assisted features. The service is provided on an “as available” basis during preview and general availability phases.

sections.title: Accounts
sections.content: You sign in through Janua (auth.madfam.io). You are responsible for activity under your account and for maintaining the confidentiality of your session. Notify us promptly of unauthorized access.

sections.title: Acceptable use
sections.content: Do not misuse Voxa to harass others, upload illegal content, attempt to bypass security, or interfere with service operation. Do not use generated symbols or speech output to impersonate others or violate applicable law.

sections.title: Content and ownership
sections.content: You retain ownership of boards and media you upload. You grant MADFAM a limited license to host, sync, and display that content solely to operate the service. Open Board Format export remains available to avoid lock-in.

sections.title: Clinical disclaimer
sections.content: Voxa is not a medical device unless explicitly labeled and cleared as such. It does not provide diagnosis or treatment. Clinicians remain responsible for assessment and therapy decisions.

sections.title: Paid plans
sections.content: When billing is enabled through MADFAM (Dhanam), subscription terms, refunds, and taxes will be presented at checkout. Free tiers may have usage limits.

sections.title: Termination
sections.content: You may stop using Voxa at any time. We may suspend access for violations of these terms or to protect the platform. Upon termination, export your boards where possible before account closure.

sections.title: Limitation of liability
sections.content: To the maximum extent permitted by law, MADFAM is not liable for indirect or consequential damages. Our aggregate liability is limited to fees paid in the twelve months before the claim, or fifty US dollars if no fees were paid.

sections.title: Governing law
sections.content: These terms are governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, USA, without regard to conflict-of-law rules, except where mandatory consumer protections apply in your jurisdiction.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.intro: Voxa targets WCAG 2.2 Level AA and AAC-specific accessibility beyond baseline web requirements. We welcome feedback from communicators, caregivers, and SLPs.

sections.title: Conformance target
sections.content: We design for WCAG 2.2 Level AA including target size (2.5.8), pointer alternatives (2.5.7), contrast, and keyboard operability. AAC buttons default to at least 1 cm × 1 cm with user-adjustable scaling.

sections.title: AAC-specific features
sections.content: Voxa includes CVI themes; switch scanning (one or two switches, row and quadrant groups, acceptance time); dwell selection that works with any device that moves the pointer, including head pointers and eye trackers whose own software drives the pointer (Voxa has no direct eye-tracker hardware integration); a tap-to-move alternative to dragging buttons in the editor; and motor-planning grid locks. See docs/accessibility.md in our repository for engineering details.

sections.title: Known limitations
sections.content: Third-party symbol images may lack alternative text if imported from external boards. Some AI prediction features require connectivity. Mobile apps are catching up to web accessibility parity.

sections.title: Assessment approach
sections.content: Automated axe checks run in CI on the public pages and on the communicator in each board theme; switch scanning is tested with keyboard-emulating switches. We have not yet tested with eye-tracker hardware.

sections.title: Feedback
sections.content: Email hola@madfam.io with the page or feature, assistive technology used, and steps to reproduce barriers. We aim to respond within five business days.

symbols.title: Symbol credits
symbols.intro: The pictograms Voxa shows are Mulberry Symbols. This page credits their author and licence, as the licence requires.

sections.title: Mulberry Symbols
sections.content: Mulberry Symbols © Steve Lee, licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0). Voxa includes the complete set unmodified (version 3.6.1, 3,436 symbols) and serves it from its own servers.

sections.title: Search keywords
sections.content: English and French names and the categories come from the Mulberry Symbols metadata (same licence). The Spanish keywords were prepared by the Voxa project for the core vocabulary and the most common words; they are pending review by a credentialed speech-language pathologist. The search index is published under CC BY-SA 4.0.

sections.title: Your own photos
sections.content: Photos you upload remain yours. Voxa only shows them on your boards and includes them when you export those boards.

sections.title: Exports
sections.content: When you export a board as OBF or OBZ, every Mulberry symbol carries its licence notice (CC BY-SA 4.0, Steve Lee, links to the licence and the source), so you can share it in line with the licence.

sections.title: Earlier symbols
sections.content: Boards created before October 2026 could use pictograms from another library whose licence allows non-commercial use only. Voxa no longer shows, searches or exports them: those cells show their text only and the editor asks you to choose a new symbol.

sections.title: Code
sections.content: Voxa's code is published under the Apache 2.0 licence. The symbols and the search index keep their CC BY-SA 4.0 licence.
